question: What is the primary goal of a School Health Programme?

options.A: To diagnose and treat chronic adult illnesses
options.B: To provide free accommodation for teachers
options.C: To replace local hospitals within rural communities
options.D: To promote and protect the well-being of students and staff

explanation: The core purpose of the programme is safeguarding the physical, mental, and social health of the school population. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why are schools considered ideal settings for health promotion?

options.A: Teachers are formally trained as medical doctors
options.B: Children spend a large portion of their formative years there
options.C: Schools have unlimited financial budgets for healthcare
options.D: Students are already immune to most childhood diseases

explanation: Gathering children in one place makes it easier to deliver preventive services and teach healthy habits consistently. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h1)

question: Which service is a primary responsibility within school health services?

options.B: Routine health screenings and first aid

explanation: School nurses focus on preventive checks, early detection, and managing minor injuries or emergencies on site. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h2)

question: A student is found to have a severe heart murmur during a routine school check. What is the most appropriate next step?

options.A: Ignore the finding since the child looks healthy
options.B: Refer the student to a specialized pediatric clinic
options.C: Instruct the class teacher to prescribe medication
options.D: Send the child home permanently from school

explanation: Serious conditions detected during school screenings require formal referral to medical specialists for proper diagnosis and management. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h2)

question: Which factor represents part of the physical school health environment?

options.A: Safe water supply and clean toilets
options.B: The political climate of the community
options.C: The emotional stability of the principal
options.D: The grading system used for examinations

explanation: Physical components refer to tangible structures and amenities like safe drinking water, ventilation, and sanitation facilities. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h3)

question: A school has broken sewage pipes near the cafeteria and many students are presenting with diarrhea. Which component of the health programme has failed?
explanation: Broken sewage and contaminated surroundings represent a breakdown in the physical and sanitary school environment. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of health education in schools?

options.A: To train students to become qualified medical doctors
options.B: To fill up empty timetable periods with lectures
options.C: To promote positive behavioral changes and healthy habits
options.D: To replace practical nursing clinical rotations

explanation: Health education aims to give students the knowledge and attitude needed to adopt healthy lifestyles. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why are interactive methods like role-play preferred over lecturing for school health instruction?

options.A: They guarantee that students will never fall ill
options.B: They require no preparation from the classroom teacher
options.C: Children prefer reading long medical textbooks
options.D: They actively engage students and improve practical habits

explanation: Interactive learning helps students internalize concepts and apply them to real-life situations better than passive listening. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h4)

question: What is a primary benefit of school feeding programmes?

options.A: Improving student concentration and cognitive development
options.B: Increasing the school fees paid by parents
options.C: Replacing the role of parents in family budgeting
options.D: Eliminating the need for any teaching staff

explanation: Adequate nutrition provides the energy and nutrients required for active learning and brain development. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h5)

question: Which activity is an appropriate duty for a nurse within the school nutrition service?

options.A: Fixing broken gas cookers in the school kitchen
options.B: Screening students for physical signs of malnutrition
options.C: Cooking meals for the entire primary section
options.D: Purchasing food ingredients from local open markets

explanation: Nurses are trained to assess nutritional status and identify clinical signs of deficiencies like stunting or anemia. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h5)

question: Why is staff health considered a key component of the School Health Programme?

options.A: Staff members consume the majority of school meals
options.B: Adults are more prone to infections than young children
options.C: Teachers are legally required to work twenty-four hours daily
options.D: Healthy staff serve as role models and maintain productivity

explanation: Staff well-being directly impacts the quality of teaching and ensures that adults model healthy behaviors for students. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h6)

question: Which intervention directly supports the occupational health of school teachers?

options.A: Requiring teachers to grade papers overnight without rest
options.B: Reducing their salaries to encourage financial discipline
options.C: Abolishing all staff lounge and rest facilities
options.D: Providing ergonomic seating and stress management workshops

explanation: Ergonomics and mental health support protect teachers from physical strain and burnout associated with their jobs. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h6)

question: Who is a key partner in sustaining school health initiatives within the local area?
explanation: PTAs connect the school with parents and community members who provide vital support and resources for health projects. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h7)

question: Why is collaboration between schools and local primary health centers important?

options.A: It creates a smooth referral pathway for immunization and clinical care
options.B: It allows the school to take over full control of the clinic
options.C: It stops community members from seeking traditional medicine
options.D: It ensures that students never have to visit a hospital again

explanation: Local health centers provide backup support for vaccination drives, medical referrals, and complex treatments beyond school capacity. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h7)

question: What is the primary difference between monitoring and evaluation in a health programme?

options.A: Monitoring focuses on finances, evaluation on food quality
options.B: Monitoring is continuous, while evaluation is periodic
options.C: Monitoring is done by students, evaluation by government
options.D: Evaluation costs nothing, while monitoring is very expensive

explanation: Monitoring happens constantly during implementation, whereas evaluation assesses overall results at specific milestones. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h8)

question: Why do health coordinators analyze student clinic attendance records during a programme evaluation?

options.A: To punish students who visit the nurse too frequently
options.B: To calculate the exact salaries of the school nurses
options.C: To determine which textbooks are best for mathematics
options.D: To measure the success of preventive measures and identify trends

explanation: Clinic records reveal patterns of illness, helping teams evaluate whether health interventions are reducing disease incidence. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h8)
